title: The Bright Terminal
premise: Freya Lockridge, a clone of a murdered courier, inherits both the dead woman's route and her unsolved case, running cargo between worlds that severed diplomatic ties generations ago. When a distress signal arrives in a language extinct for two centuries, Freya realizes the original was killed because she found the same transmission—and that the killer's heirs still control the relay at the edge of dead space. Racing the closing jump window, Freya must decode the signal, which reveals that the 'extinct' language belongs to survivors hiding in the dark, and that the Lockridge fortune was built on their betrayal. In the end, Freya broadcasts the truth to both worlds, forfeits the inheritance, and chooses the long route as her own person—neither the original's shadow nor her killer's legacy.
about_author: Kestrel Nakamura is a former maritime radio operator who spent six years relaying messages across the North Pacific before turning to fiction. Their novels explore inherited debts and the voices that refuse to go silent.

chapters.title: The Inheritance Clause
chapters.summary: Freya, awakened into the original's life, reads the will that names her heir and case-holder. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: disorientation curdling into grim resolve as she realizes the inheritance is a burden disguised as a gift.

chapters.title: Manifest of the Dead
chapters.summary: Sorting the original's effects, Freya finds a corrupted data-slate referencing an 'unsent message.' POV: Freya. Emotional beat: unease—the original knew she was going to die.

chapters.title: First Jump
chapters.summary: Freya runs the route solo for the first time, learning the ship's ghosts and the original's muscle-memory habits. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: loneliness tempered by the strange intimacy of flying another woman's hands.

chapters.title: The Silent Ports
chapters.summary: Docking at a waystation split between the two estranged worlds, Freya observes the embargo's human cost. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: anger at the politics that made the long route necessary.

chapters.title: Signal in the Dark
chapters.summary: Deep-space sensors catch a repeating burst—phonemes from a language declared extinct two centuries ago. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: awe and dread; the original's slate flickers to life in response.

chapters.title: What the Slate Knew
chapters.summary: Deciphering the original's partial notes, Freya learns she had decoded fragments and contacted someone before dying. POV: Freya with slate-voice interludes. Emotional beat: grief for a woman she was cloned from, whom she never met.

chapters.title: The Detective's Heir
chapters.summary: Freya contacts the original's old ally, a retired investigator, who warns her the murder case was closed too neatly. POV: alternating Freya/investigator. Emotional beat: cautious alliance.

chapters.title: Heirs Apparent
chapters.summary: The Lockridge family's other beneficiaries arrive, demanding the slate and offering to buy her out. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: threat wearing a friendly face; Freya refuses.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Her drive coils are found tampered with; the ship barely makes orbit. POV: ship's AI, newly awakened. Emotional beat: the first proof someone wants her dead like the original.

chapters.title: The Extinct Tongue
chapters.summary: A linguist in the embargo zone helps Freya decode more: the signal is a census, a count of living survivors. POV: linguist. Emotional beat: hope—the dead language has living speakers.

chapters.title: Ledger of Betrayal
chapters.summary: Freya uncovers records showing the Lockridge fortune funded the purge that 'extincted' the language. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: horror; her inheritance is blood money.

chapters.title: The Offer
chapters.summary: The family's fixer makes a final offer: silence, wealth, and the truth of who killed the original. POV: fixer. Emotional beat: temptation and contempt; Freya realizes the killer's identity is bait.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Waypoint
chapters.summary: Pursuers force Freya off the sanctioned route into dead space proper. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: terror and a strange freedom—off the map, no one owns her.

chapters.title: Voices in the Static
chapters.summary: Following the signal's source, Freya receives a direct transmission: the survivors, watching her approach. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: being seen for the first time as herself, not the original.

chapters.title: The Survivor Station
chapters.summary: Freya docks with a hidden station of descendants who preserved the language and remember the Lockridge name. POV: station elder. Emotional beat: grief, accusation, and the question of whether Freya is heir or accomplice.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Message
chapters.summary: The station recovered the original's final transmission before her death: she had promised to broadcast their existence. POV: recording/original. Emotional beat: Freya inherits a promise, not just a debt.

chapters.title: Jump Window
chapters.summary: The relay's alignment opens a narrow window to reach the inter-world antenna; the family's ships are inbound. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the race begins—hours, not days.

chapters.title: Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: Freya fights through the relay's defenses to the antenna core, the fixer's ship on her tail. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: desperation sharpening into clarity.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax: Freya transmits the census, the ledger, and the original's message to both worlds simultaneously. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: the moment of choice—she could still stop, and doesn't.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: The fixer boards; Freya confronts her with the evidence that the family ordered both murders. POV: Freya and fixer. Emotional beat: justice outside the law—the truth itself is the verdict.

chapters.title: After the Signal
chapters.summary: The broadcast forces both worlds to open negotiations; the family's assets are frozen; the survivors emerge. POV: multiple brief voices. Emotional beat: the world changing because one voice refused silence.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Freya, renouncing the inheritance, registers the ship under her own name and takes a contract to carry the first official mail between the reconciled worlds. POV: Freya. Emotional beat: quiet joy—an identity chosen, a route that is finally hers.
